speaker_role: independent counselor (Craig Meister, college admissions coach, CollegeMeister)
commercial_incentive: yes - explicitly promotes his one-on-one paid admissions coaching at collegemeister.com
key_insights: Argues that 'holistic admissions,' though marketed as an even-handed 360-degree evaluation of every applicant, functions in practice as a mechanism for colleges to hit specific institutional targets rather than simply reward individual merit.

Cites a real internal email from Boston University's Dean of Admissions/AVP of Enrollment, sent to counselors after the class of 2028's first admissions cycle following the Supreme Court's ruling ending race-conscious admissions, stating BU 'remains committed' to a diverse class and will continue this 'by continuing to practice holistic admissions' to identify students whose varied experiences and talents contribute to the university community.
Interprets that email as evidence that, at least at BU, 'holistic' review is being used post-SFFA v. Harvard as a race-neutral proxy mechanism to preserve student body diversity outcomes.

Argues that because the institution defines what counts as valuable/diverse, holistic review effectively means the college scans applications for whatever unstated characteristics it has already decided it wants, rather than rewarding applicants purely on individual merit.
Suggests it would benefit applicants if colleges published explicit lists of what they value and in what proportions, rather than using the vaguer language of holistic review.
References an upcoming (unreleased in this video) analysis of Duke's admissions practices as further illustration of subjective, non-standardized evaluation criteria.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Quotes a Boston University admissions leadership email to counselors (unnamed sender/title given only as 'associate vice president of enrollment and Dean of admissions') stating BU is 'committed to attracting and enrolling a diverse student body' via 'continuing to practice holistic admissions,' sent after the first admissions cycle affected by the Supreme Court's ban on race-conscious admissions
notable_or_distinctive: Builds its entire argument around a specific quoted internal counselor email from a named university's admissions leadership, using it as evidence for a broader, more skeptical theory about what 'holistic admissions' really means post-affirmative-action.
reliability_notes: The video is largely the speaker's own interpretive argument/opinion built from a single quoted email rather than documented policy or multiple data points; it is speculative editorializing presented with strong rhetorical certainty, and should be treated as one consultant's critical theory rather than verified institutional practice.
